question: Why do opposite-sign deviations produce negative covariance?
direct_answer: Because a positive deviation times a negative deviation is negative.
expanded_answer: When one variable is above its mean and the other is below its mean, their centered deviations have opposite signs. Multiplying them gives a negative product, so such pairs contribute negatively to covariance.
key_points: This reflects opposite movement relative to the mean
Many such pairs push covariance below zero
common_wrong_ideas: Negative covariance means the variables are unrelated
One negative pair always determines the whole covariance
